Passenger · United States

Arland D. Williams Jr.

Air Florida Flight 901982
Flight
Air Florida Flight 90
Date
13 January 1982
Aircraft
Boeing 737-200
Location
Potomac River, Washington, D.C.
Survivors
5 of 79 aboard

After the crash into the icy Potomac River, he repeatedly passed the rescue helicopter's lifeline to other survivors. He drowned before he could be rescued himself.

Who helped

  • Donald W. Usher U.S. Park Police helicopter pilot (Eagle 1)Flew the Park Police helicopter low over the icy river, at times with its skids in the water, to tow survivors to shore.Sources: 1 2 3 4 5
  • Melvin E. "Gene" Windsor U.S. Park Police rescue technician (Eagle 1)Dropped lines to survivors from the helicopter, then stood on its skid to grab a weakened woman from the water and hold her as they flew to shore.Sources: 1 2 3 4 5
  • Lenny Skutnik Bystander (Congressional Budget Office employee)Took off his coat and boots, jumped into the icy Potomac and swam out to pull Priscilla Tirado, too weak to hold the line, to shore.Sources: 1 2 3 4 5 6
  • Roger Olian Bystander (sheet-metal worker)Tied a rope around himself and went into the ice-filled river to try to reach the survivors, staying in the water until the helicopter arrived.Sources: 1 2 3 4
  • Kelly Duncan Flight attendantThe only surviving crew member, she inflated the one life vest the survivors could find and gave it to a badly injured passenger.Sources: 1 2 3 4

Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Florida_Flight_90 ↗
